title: Bhakti Movement Groups Alvars
definition: The Alvars were a group of 12 Tamil poet-saints who lived between the 6th and 9th centuries CE, dedicated to the path of 'Bhakti' (devotion) towards Lord Vishnu (Vishnu-bhakti). They were instrumental in the revival of Hinduism in South India, challenging the dominance of Jainism and Buddhism through emotional, vernacular poetry.
importanceInUpsc: UPSC frequently tests the distinction between Alvars (Vaishnavite) and Nayanars (Shaivite), their social inclusivity (caste/gender), and their literary contributions (Divya Prabandham).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Bhakti Movement Groups Alvars.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of South Indian history (Pallava/Pandya period)
General knowledge of Vedic vs. Bhakti traditions
